title: Search text without letter case
summary: ILIKE is PostgreSQL's case-insensitive pattern match.
introduction: ILIKE is PostgreSQL's case-insensitive pattern match. Your task: Change the pattern to garden%.
learningObjectives: Explain the example for search text without letter case

blocks.text: ILIKE is PostgreSQL's case-insensitive pattern match. A percent sign matches any length of text.
Use PostgreSQL in a new practice database through psql or a database editor. These are PostgreSQL examples, not SQLite. They do not run in this site's SQL playground. Use only sample data.

blocks.code:
WITH books(title) AS (VALUES ('Moon Trip'),('Garden Days'))
SELECT title FROM books WHERE title ILIKE 'moon%';
blocks.title: Search text without letter case

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: `ILIKE` is PostgreSQL's case-insensitive pattern match. `%` matches a run of any text.
`SELECT` names the output values. `AS` can give a calculated result a readable column name.
`WHERE` keeps only rows that pass its condition. Check the condition with sample data before using it for a change.

blocks.text: The result contains Moon Trip even though the pattern begins with lowercase moon.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: ILIKE is not standard in every SQL engine. Use the PostgreSQL tool for this syntax.
